# `nish`

`"nish"`: what a host module (the page's TypeScript) imports its widths from, `import type { f64, i32, HostHandle } from "nish"`. The package's root `types` entry is this file, which is how the page's `tsc` finds the module. The widths are the page's reading of them, which is the loader's: an `i64` or `u64` crosses as a `bigint`, every other width as a `number`.

```ts
import {
  HostHandle,
  f32,
  f64,
  i32,
  i64,
  integer,
  u16,
  u32,
  u64,
  u8,
} from "nish";
```

## HostHandle

```ts
type HostHandle<K extends string> = number & reflection | 0
```

## f32

```ts
type f32 = number
```

## f64

```ts
type f64 = number
```

## i32

```ts
type i32 = number
```

## i64

```ts
type i64 = bigint
```

## integer

A ranged integer, which the loader checks on the way in.

```ts
type integer<Lo extends number, Hi extends number> = number
```

```ts
type u16 = number
```
